newsitem.title: GERMANY: Analysts say Lufthansa fall overdone.
newsitem.headline: Analysts say Lufthansa fall overdone.

text.p: Airline analysts said on Tuesday the sharp dive in Germany's Deutsche Lufthansa AG shares following the publication of proposals for foreign share ownership limits were overdone.
CHRIS TARRY, KLEINWORT BENSON, LONDON: "Anybody who's been following Lufthansa for any time should not be concerned by this at all.

"People are over-reacting to the risk of forced sales (of Lufthansa shares), which is not an immediate issue at all. In 10 years, British Airways has not got close to its limit (which sets out similar foreign ownership restrictions)."
JUERGEN POELLMAN, BAYERISCHE VEREINSBANK, MUNICH: "Concern that foreign investors could in some way be shut out has affected the sentiment today, but fundamentally there is no impact on its shares.

"Similar systems for dealing (non-freely transferable) registered shares exist already, for example for some of the shares in (German reinsurance giant) Munich Re. In the past, these systems have been a bit awkward, but it has not resulted in any noticeable drag on Munich Re's shares.
